object_description: elongated stepped volume, three storeys dropping to two towards the north-east
design_condition: the long body along the street defines a square-like outdoor space opposite the existing building and steps down in the visual axis of the monastery, sitting on the topographical edge of the playing field

positive: Defines a connecting, square-like outdoor space opposite the existing building
Alignment and height development elegantly mediate between the neighbouring buildings
The piazza interprets the intersecting movement axes and becomes a credible prelude to the main entrance
The inner hall spanned by two single-flight staircases connects the square level with the higher hard court level
The layered spatial structure leads to a harmonious disposition of uses across all three storeys
Floor-to-ceiling openings let the ground floor studios enliven the public space
The main floor plan logic meaningfully groups and structures the different usage groups
Diagonal spatial relations overlap with the central light and air space of the hall
The layering principle produces a structurally stable falsework offering a sensible degree of flexibility
The varied facade theme develops an expression that thematizes the all-round orientation
negative: The almost symmetrical circulation area does not get optimal daylight everywhere, making orientation difficult
The roof area created by the stepping is not used as a terrace because the top storey holds only administration
The stepped structure combined with the length and height of the building appears problematic in the built context
The fine facade grid requires internal wall connections to be intercepted by closed window elements, which is not convincing outside
The proposal to ensure natural ventilation via a tilt mechanism provides food for discussion
Building costs are in the upper range
